name: JavaScript
summary: The language of the web: logic, interactivity and talking to servers — including the event loop everything else in it rests on.
prerequisites: No previous programming required. HTML and CSS are not assumed either, though everything here ends up on a page.
syllabus: Modern syntax (ES6+), types, coercion and scope
Functions, closures, `this` and the prototype chain
Asynchrony: the event loop, promises, async/await and fetch
Browser web APIs: storage, geolocation, notifications
Modules, package managers and debugging in the browser
topics: ES6+ syntax: let/const, arrow functions and template strings
Types, coercion, strict equality and falsy values
Hoisting, the temporal dead zone, and why `var` behaves differently
Objects, arrays, spread and destructuring
Keyed collections: Map, Set, WeakMap and WeakSet
Functions, scope, closures and the value of `this`
call, apply, bind, and borrowing a function
Classes, prototypes and the prototype chain
ES modules, CommonJS, and what changed between them
Iterators and generators
DOM: selecting, creating and changing elements
Events, bubbling, delegation and forms
The event loop: call stack, task queue and microtasks
Asynchrony: callbacks, promises and async/await
Timers: setTimeout, setInterval, and what "zero" really means
fetch, JSON and handling network errors
Errors: throw, try/catch/finally and the Error objects
Web APIs: localStorage, sessionStorage, geolocation and notifications
Memory: lifecycle, garbage collection and the leaks you cause
Strict mode, and the sharp edges it turns off
npm, pnpm and yarn: installing, versioning and publishing packages
Debugging in the browser: breakpoints, the profiler and the network tab
